input.title: BH | Premier Samos Quilted Leather Armchair
input.descriptionHtml:
Samos, the green Greek island where Pythagoras was born, has a light that makes everyone slow down: long afternoons indoors with the shutters half closed, a cool drink and a good chair to sink into. This armchair is made for those afternoons. Its seat runs deep enough to settle back into, and its arms sit at an easy height to rest a glass or an elbow.

It is upholstered in top grain leather over a sturdy frame, a leather that softens and warms the more the chair is used. The 17-inch seat height keeps it low and relaxed, with arms at 24 inches, and at 31 inches wide it fits a corner or a window bay where a bulkier chair would crowd the room. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in a living room corner beside a window, with a side table for a cold drink, a lamp and a stack of books, or set two facing each other across a low table for conversation. This listing is for one armchair.

input.title: BH | Premier Tavistock Leather Wing Chair — In Cognac
input.descriptionHtml:
Tavistock sits on the western edge of Dartmoor, and after a day walking the moor among granite tors and wild ponies, the reward is a high-backed chair by the fire and a book on your knee. This wing chair is made for that reward. Its wings, the side panels that rise above the arms, shelter you from drafts and frame your head as you read, and its tall back lets you sink in for a whole chapter.

It is upholstered in full grain leather, the toughest and most natural layer of the hide, which keeps its true character and softens over the years. Antique brass nailheads trace its outline, and the seat is 22 inches deep for settling well back, while its 17-inch seat height makes it easy to drop into after a long day on foot. Assembly is required.

Set it beside the fireplace in a study or living room, with a reading lamp behind your shoulder, a small table for tea and a wool throw over one wing. This listing is for one wing chair.

input.title: BH | Premier New Haven Leather Swivel Desk Chair
input.descriptionHtml:
New Haven has been Yale's home since 1716, and the town runs on long hours at a desk: a lamp on, papers spread, a chair that turns to reach a book from the shelf behind. This desk chair is made for those long hours. It swivels freely and rolls on five casters, so you can move from desk to bookshelf without getting up, and its leather seat and arms invite you to sit back between pages.

It is upholstered in leather over a metal frame, set on a five-pronged swivel base. The seat is 19 inches high and 19 deep, with arms at 25 inches, a comfortable shape for a full day's work, and the leather softens gently as it is used.

Pull it up to a writing desk in a study or home office, with a brass lamp, a stack of notebooks and a mug of coffee, or use it at a library table spread with maps, letters and the household accounts. This listing is for one desk chair.

input.title: BH | Premier Hay-on-Wye Tufted Leather Armchair — In Cognac
input.descriptionHtml:
Since Richard Booth began filling Hay-on-Wye with secondhand books in the 1960s, the little town on the border of Wales and England has been a place to buy an armful of books and then find somewhere to sit and read them. This armchair is made for that second part. Its high back is shaped to rest your head against, and its arms rise high enough to prop a book on through a long chapter.

It is upholstered in top grain leather, deeply tufted across the back, and finished with brass nailheads that trace its lines. It stands on wooden legs, with castors on the front pair so the chair rolls easily toward the lamp or the fire. Its 20-inch seat depth gives room to settle back properly, and it arrives fully assembled.

Angle it into the corner of a study or library under a good reading lamp, with a side table close by for a mug of tea and the stack of books still to be read. This listing is for one armchair.

input.title: BH | Premier Ketchum Leather Armchair — In Cognac
input.descriptionHtml:
In a Ketchum house after a day on the trails above the Wood River, the evening belongs to a big leather chair, a glass of something and a long read before the fire. This armchair is made for settling into after a day outdoors. It is wide and deep, with a 21-inch seat and broad arms to rest on, and it rolls on castors, so it can be drawn closer to the hearth as the night gets colder.

The leather is aniline, a top grade cowhide finished to show its natural grain, and it softens and takes on a patina the longer it is used. Nailhead trim outlines the frame, which is made of wood. The seat sits 19 inches high and the arms 24, so a book rests comfortably on them. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it by the hearth in a den, angled toward a lamp, with a side table close by for a drink and a stack of books, and a leather ottoman in front for your feet. This listing is for one armchair.

Dulwich is a leafy London village, home since 1817 to the first purpose-built public art gallery in England, and its quiet houses suit a particular pleasure: an afternoon in the study with a book, a lamp on and the street outside going about its business without you. This armchair is made for the reading hour. Its seat sits at a comfortable 19 inches, its arms at a height where an open book can rest, and its leather invites you to stay for another chapter.

It is upholstered in top grain leather over a dark hardwood frame and feet, with brass nailheads tracing its outline, the look of a chair found at a Paris flea market and brought home. The leather is the kind that softens and darkens gently with years of use. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in the corner of a study or library beside a floor lamp, with a low table at its elbow holding a teacup and tomorrow's book, or set a pair on either side of a fireplace. This listing is for one armchair.

input.descriptionHtml:
In a great house of the early 1600s like Hatfield, finished in 1611, the warmest place on a winter evening was always a seat by the fire. The wing chair grew out of that need in late seventeenth-century England, its tall sides made to keep drafts off the sitter and hold the warmth of the hearth. This chair is made for that same place by the fire. Its broad wings wrap around your shoulders, and its flared arms give you somewhere to rest a book or a glass.

Its top grain leather has a deep, rich patina, the arms flared out and finished in a vertical roll, and brass nailheads in an aged finish trace its outline. It stands on a walnut base, and at 44 inches tall its back rises well above the shoulders of most sitters. It needs light assembly.

Set it beside the fireplace in a living room or library, with a reading lamp behind it, a small table for a whisky or a cup of tea, and a footstool in front. This listing is for one wing chair.

Give it pride of place in a large living room, a library or a generous hall, with a reading lamp nearby, a low table for coffee cups and room for people to come and go around it. This listing is for one sofa.

This lounge chair is made for that kind of leaning back. Its low 16-inch seat lets you sink down and stretch your legs out, and its leather, held in a gleaming steel frame, has the clean modern lines of an apartment above the lake.

It is upholstered in aniline cowhide, leather dyed right through and left without a heavy surface coat, so it stays soft and shows the natural markings of the hide. The frame is stainless steel in a bright silver finish, and the 26-inch-wide seat gives room to shift and settle. The chair arrives fully assembled.

Set it by a window with a floor lamp and a small table for an espresso and a book, or pair two in a living room, angled toward the view with a low table between them for the afternoon paper. This listing is for one lounge chair.

This swivel chair lets you choose your view in the same way. It turns easily toward the window, the fire or the conversation, and its rounded barrel back wraps around you, so you can curl up with a book rather than sit up straight.

It is covered in top grain leather and channel tufted, with deep vertical grooves stitched into the back, which give it a tailored shape and a soft, fluted feel against your shoulders. At 32 inches across it is compact enough for a bedroom corner or a small living room. It arrives fully assembled.

Set a pair facing a window in a living room with a small table between them for coffee cups, or put one in a bedroom corner with a lamp and a pile of novels. This listing is for one swivel chair.

input.descriptionHtml:
Gray's Inn has been home to London barristers since the 1300s, and the work there still happens at a desk: papers spread out, a brief to read, and a chair that turns from the desk to the bookshelves and back again. This office chair is made for that kind of work. It swivels and rolls on five castors, so you can reach the shelf or the printer without standing, and its leather seat stays comfortable through a long afternoon of reading.

It is upholstered in top grain cow leather over a metal frame, and a lever releases the back so you can lean back and think between tasks. Arms at 29 inches give your forearms somewhere to rest while you read, and the 21-inch seat height suits a standard desk. It needs simple assembly when it arrives.

Pull it up to a desk in a home office or study, with a lamp, a stack of files and a cup of tea at one elbow, or use it at a writing table in the corner of a bedroom. This listing is for one office chair.

input.descriptionHtml:
Woodhall Spa grew up around its spa waters in Victorian and Edwardian times, a Lincolnshire village of woodland walks where visitors came for nothing more demanding than rest. This leather recliner is made for that same purpose at home. Lean back and it reclines fully, supporting you from head to toe, so a long afternoon with your feet up becomes the easiest part of the day.

It is upholstered in top grain cowhide with antique brass nailheads tracing its lines, over a frame of rubberwood, a dense, stable hardwood. The leather grows softer and richer in tone over years of use, and the nailheads give the chair a tailored, traditional finish that suits a study or library as well as a den. It is delivered in two boxes and needs assembly.

Place it in a den facing the screen, or by the fire in a living room, with a side table for a cup of tea and the remote close by. This listing is for one recliner.

Put a pair by a bay window in a living room or a sunroom, with a small table between them for a pot of tea, or use one in a den or a bedroom corner for reading. This listing is for one armchair.

input.title: BH | Premier Sagamore Hill Leather Recliner — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
At Sagamore Hill, the house above Oyster Bay that the twenty-sixth president called home, the busiest days ended in a library lined with books and trophies, where the letters were answered and a long read waited. This recliner is made for that well-earned end of the day. It has the broad, square shape of a traditional club chair, and it leans back into a full recline that supports you from your head to your heels.

It is upholstered in cowhide leather over a rubberwood frame, a dense hardwood that keeps its strength through years of use, and the leather softens the more the chair is used. At 39 inches wide and 38 inches deep it is a generous chair, with room to turn and settle in with a book for the whole evening. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Set it in a study or library by the window, with a reading lamp, a side table stacked with biographies and a glass of something within reach, or in a den facing the fire. This listing is for one recliner.

This chair is made for settling in like that. Its seat runs 22 inches deep, its back angles in at the sides to hold you, and its slim arms leave room to talk with your hands.

It is upholstered in aniline cowhide, leather dyed through and left soft, over a wood frame, and the seat cushion is welted, its seams finished with a neat piped edge. Nailhead trim runs along the frame. The seat is 20 inches high and the arms 24, an easy, relaxed height for a lounge chair. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in a den or by the fireplace in a cabin living room, with a side table for a glass, a lamp for the fishing magazines and a wool blanket over the back. This listing is for one armchair.

It is upholstered in top grain cow leather over a rubberwood frame, with fine self-welting, a slim piping cut from the same leather, along its edges. The seat cushion is T-shaped, reaching forward beside the arms for extra room, and it stands on straight legs. The 20-inch seat height and 21-inch seat depth make a comfortable sit. It needs some assembly.

Place it beside the fireplace with a reading lamp, a small table for tea and a blanket over the arm, or in a bedroom corner for reading late, with a stack of novels on the floor beside it. This listing is for one wing chair.

input.title: BH | Premier Peebles Leather Barrel-Back Armchair
input.descriptionHtml:
Peebles sits on the River Tweed in the Scottish Borders, and a good day there ends with a long walk by the water, then a chair by the fire with a book and a dram. This armchair is made for that well-earned sit. Its winged barrel back curves around you to keep drafts off your shoulders, and its exposed wooden arms give your hands a warm, solid rest while you turn the pages.

It is covered in top grain leather, tufted lightly across the back, and its legs are tipped in brass, a neat detail down at floor level. Its curved back and 30-inch width give it a compact, enveloping shape that suits a smaller room or a corner. The leather grows softer with every winter by the fire. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside the fire in a living room or study, with a side table for a glass and a lamp over your shoulder, or pair two across a small table. This listing is for one armchair.

input.title: BH | Premier Hay-on-Wye Leather and Jute Armchair — In Cognac with Natural Jute
input.descriptionHtml:
Each year the Hay Festival fills Hay-on-Wye with writers and readers, and between the talks every comfortable chair in town is taken by someone already halfway into a book bought that morning. This armchair is made for that kind of reading. Its deep buttoning holds you comfortably upright, its back rises tall enough to lean into, and its arms are set high enough to prop an elbow while the pages turn.

The leather is aniline, dyed right through rather than coated, so it feels soft from the first day and grows more supple with use. The outside back is covered in jute, a coarse natural weave that sets off the leather, and the chair stands on turned wooden legs with castors at the front. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it a place by a window in a study or a bedroom corner, with a footstool, a reading lamp and a short stack of new books on the floor beside it. This listing is for one armchair.

input.title: BH | Premier Hay-on-Wye Tufted Leather Wing Chair
input.descriptionHtml:
The wing chair was made in England in the late 1600s for sitting close to the fire, its tall sides keeping off drafts while the reader inside stayed warm. In Hay-on-Wye, the town of books on the border of Wales and England, that is still the best way to spend a wet afternoon. This wing chair is made for it, with wings to tuck into and arms that hold a book at a comfortable height.

It is upholstered in aniline leather, coloured right through rather than coated, tufted across the back and edged with a line of brass nailheads. The front legs run on castors, so it rolls easily toward the light, and its 20-inch seat depth lets you sit well back. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside the hearth in a study or a book-lined den, with a side table for a lamp and a glass, and a basket of books within reach. A pair facing each other makes a reading corner for two. This listing is for one wing chair.

Set it by a desk in a study or library, or angled toward the fire in a living room, with a side table for a glass, a reading lamp at its shoulder and a basket of newspapers within reach. This listing is for one swivel chair.

The frame is American oak, and the upholstery is pigskin, a supple leather with a fine natural grain, given an antiqued finish so it looks lived in from the first day. A line of nailheads finishes the edges. Its 17-inch seat sits low and relaxed, the easy height of a lounge chair, and the seat runs 21 inches deep. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in a bedroom or study corner with a floor lamp, a side table and a stack of novels, or pair two across a small table for coffee and conversation. This listing is for one armchair.

This armchair is made for that well-earned rest. Its back rises into a headrest, so you can let your head go and close your eyes, and its arms sit at 24 inches, just right for resting a glass.

It is upholstered in aniline cow leather, leather dyed right through with no surface coating, so it shows its natural markings and grows richer with use. The frame is wood, and the seat sits at 18 inches with 20 inches of depth, a compact, upright shape for a den or a study. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it beside the fireplace with a small table for a whiskey and a book, or at a desk in a home office where a lean back between tasks is welcome. This listing is for one armchair.

Its sculpted shape follows the egg form of mid-century Scandinavian design. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it by a fireplace or a big window in a living room or bedroom, with a sheepskin underfoot, a side table for a hot drink and a book of mountain walks, and a reading lamp angled over one shoulder for the long evenings. This listing is for one egg chair.

In the hills of Los Feliz, where Richard Neutra built the Lovell Health House in 1929, modern living meant light, air and a good chair to lounge in while the afternoon cooled. This leather chair is made for that kind of lounging. Its curved frame and low 17-inch seat settle you back rather than up, so you can stretch out your legs, and its quilted top grain leather is soft to sink into.

The leather is quilted and carried on a metal frame in a bronze finish, with oak adding warmth, a pairing of materials that suits a modernist room. The arms sit at 25 inches, an easy height to rest a book or a glass, and the oak and leather together age warmly with use. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it by a big window in a living room with a floor lamp and a side table for a drink, or pair two across from a low sofa. This listing is for one lounge chair.

Its 22-inch seat depth lets you tuck your feet up or settle well back, and its arms, at 25 inches, sit high enough to prop a book on while the pages turn.

It is upholstered in leather over a wood frame, with a line of brass nailheads in an aged finish tracing its outline, a classic detail on a shape with a cleaner, more contemporary feel. The 18-inch seat height makes it easy to sink into and just as easy to get up from when the kettle calls. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a corner of the living room or a study by a window, with a reading lamp, a side table for the tea and a basket of books on the floor beside it. This listing is for one club chair.

The old studies of a school like Eton College, founded by Henry VI in 1440, were made for one thing above all: a long read in a good chair, with the evening drawing in outside. This high-backed chair brings that habit home. Its back rises well above the shoulders, so you can rest your head when the chapter runs long, and its deep seat lets you settle back with a book open on your knee and no reason to get up.

It combines leather upholstery with a wood frame, warm and solid together. The seat is 24 inches wide and 23 inches deep, with a 19-inch seat height that is easy to rise from, and the arms sit at 23 inches, a natural height to rest a forearm or a cup. It needs some assembly.

Set it in a study or library corner with a floor lamp behind it, a side table for tea and a shelf of books within reach, or place a pair either side of a fireplace. This listing is for one armchair.

Pau became a winter retreat for British visitors in the 1800s, and its townhouses still look out from the Boulevard des Pyrénées to the mountains. On a quiet afternoon there, the best seat is a deep chair by the window with a book and the snowy peaks in view. This chair is built for that slow afternoon. Its seat is 23 inches deep, so you can sink in and stay put, and its broad frame wraps you in leather for a long chapter.

It is covered in leather over a wood frame and finished with antique brass nailheads that add a glint of old metal. The 19-inch seat height makes it easy to rise from, even after a long sit. The leather softens with use, so the chair only gets more comfortable over time. It arrives fully assembled.

Turn it toward a window in a study or angle it into a living room corner, with a lamp, a side table for coffee and a pile of novels close at hand. This listing is for one chair.

Put it by a window in a study or family room with a side table for a cup and a stack of books, or set a pair facing a sofa across a coffee table, where each can turn toward the fire or the talk. This listing is for one swivel chair.

This swivel chair is made for a room where the talk moves around you. It turns on its base to face whoever is speaking, the fire or the window, and its 22-inch seat depth and low club shape let you settle back for an evening rather than perch on the edge.

It is covered in top grain cow leather, accented with brass nailheads, and it turns on a metal swivel base built into the chair. The seat sits at 17 inches with arms at 23, low and relaxed in the club chair way, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set a pair in a living room facing a sofa, with a low table between for drinks, or put one in a study where you can turn from the desk to the fireplace. This listing is for one club chair.

This armchair is made for that kind of afternoon. At 38 inches deep it is a chair to settle into properly, with room to tuck a cushion behind you, and its leather and wood give it the look of a library.

It is upholstered in leather on a wood frame and is broad at 36 inches wide, so it has the generous proportions of a country-house chair. Leather is a lasting choice for a reading chair that gets daily use: it grows softer and more comfortable season by season. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a library or study beside a tall lamp and a side table stacked with books, or by a living room fireplace with a footstool in front for long evenings. This listing is for one armchair.

This side chair is made for that long, loose kind of meal. It has no arms, so it slides close to the table and lets people squeeze in shoulder to shoulder, and its leather seat stays comfortable through second helpings and the talk that follows.

It pairs a metal frame with wood and leather, the same mix as the armchair in this family, so the two can share a table, with armchairs at the heads and side chairs down the length. Leather is a practical seat for a dining room: spills blot away and crumbs brush off. At 24 lbs it is easy to pull out, carry and set back. It arrives fully assembled.

Set four or six around a dining table with a bowl of lemons in the middle and the plates stacked ready, or use a pair at a desk or a breakfast table by the window. This listing is for one side chair.

This club chair is made for that afternoon. It is scaled to sit comfortably without taking over a room, its seat is covered in top grain leather that softens with every read, and its arms are set low enough to rest a book on.

The frame is ash, a strong, springy hardwood, and while the seat is leather, the outer back and sides are left in jute, a natural, nubby fibre, in the deconstructed style that shows how the chair is built rather than hiding it. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a living room or sunporch by a window onto the water, with a side table for coffee and a basket of books, or make a pair facing each other for long conversations. This listing is for one club chair.

This chair is made to be that chair at home. At more than four feet wide it is generous enough to sit sideways with your legs over an arm, and its rolled arms give an elbow or a shoulder somewhere to rest.

It is covered in top grain leather in the Chesterfield manner, with neat pleats gathered at the front of each arm, and the chair sits low on legs of rubberwood. The leather grows softer with every year of use, and the chair needs light assembly when it arrives.

Set it beside the fireplace in a library or den with a reading lamp and a small table for a glass, or pair it with a Chesterfield sofa across a low table to make a club corner of your own. This listing is for one club chair.

input.title: BH | Premier Charlottenlund Leather and Iron Lounge Chair
input.descriptionHtml:
In the villas along the Øresund at Charlottenlund, north of Copenhagen, Danish modern design is simply how a room is lived in: clean lines, good leather, and a chair angled toward the water for an afternoon of doing very little. This lounge chair is made for that kind of afternoon. Its deep frame lets you sit well back, and its open, airy outline keeps the chair light to the eye in a bright room.

The leather is laid over a frame of iron, a pairing of leather and metal that Danish designers favoured from the 1950s on, and the result is a crisp contemporary silhouette that looks as good from behind as from the front. It is 25 inches wide and 36 deep, so it suits a corner or a window bay, and at 48 lbs it moves easily. It needs assembly on arrival.

Set it by a window in a living room or study, with a small side table for coffee and a magazine, or as a pair either side of a low table. This listing is for one lounge chair.

This chair is made for holding court at your own table. It pairs a frame of metal in an aged finish with aniline leather, a top grade cowhide dyed right through to keep its natural grain. Its 19-inch seat height suits a standard dining table, and at 32 lbs it is easy to draw back and pull in again. The leather darkens and softens with use, and the chair arrives fully assembled.

Set a pair at the ends of a dining table, use one at a desk in a study, or place it in a living room beside a bookshelf with a small table for a drink. This listing is for one armchair.

Its tall wings frame your head and shoulders as you read, its 23-inch seat depth lets you curl up, and its arms sit at a natural height for resting a book.

The 19-inch seat height makes it easy to sit down and rise. Linen has a relaxed, lived-in look that only improves as it softens. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it beside a fireplace or a window in a living room, study or bedroom, with a floor lamp, a footstool and a small table for the teacup. This listing is for one armchair.

In the stone cottages around Hay-on-Wye, mornings start slowly: a pot of tea, the radio turned low, and the mail read by the window before the walk up into the hills. This armchair is made for that first unhurried hour. Its seat is leather, firm and smooth for long sitting, its inside back is buttoned linen that is soft to lean against, and its arms sit high enough to rest a cup or a letter on.

The back and sides are left in jute burlap, a deconstructed finish, meaning the upholstery is left open on purpose to show the layers an upholsterer usually hides, and decorative tacks finish the edges. The wooden frame has castors on the front legs, so the chair moves easily, and the 20-inch seat lets you settle well back. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in a sunny corner of a study or bedroom with a reading lamp and a small table for a cup and the book on the go, or use a pair at either side of a bookcase. This listing is for one armchair.

It spins to face whoever is talking or playing, its rounded tub shape holds you comfortably, and its arms sit at an easy height to rest on for the whole evening.

The frame is beechwood and the body is upholstered in fabric, with a leather back cushion for contrast. From behind, the back divides into two, a split design that gives the chair a modern edge from every side of the room. Its seat is 22 inches wide, roomy enough to settle into, and it arrives fully assembled.

Place it in a living room where conversation moves around, beside a small table for a drink, or in a pair facing a sofa across a rug. This listing is for one swivel chair.

This tub chair is made for that late, warm hour. Its rounded back curves around you like an arm, and its seat is broad and low enough to sink into while the talk goes on.

The frame is beech wood, upholstered in fabric with a leather back cushion that sets off the weave. Seen from behind, the back parts into two halves, a modern touch on a classic shape. In the 1910s and 20s Diaghilev's Ballets Russes made Monte Carlo its home, and a night at the Opéra began long before curtain up, in a dressing room with a chair to sit in while shoes were buckled and cufflinks fixed. This armchair is made for getting ready like that. Its seat is firm and upright, so you can sit to fasten a shoe or keep someone company while they finish dressing, and its slim splayed legs give it a dancer's poise.

It is tightly upholstered in linen woven in houndstooth, a small broken-check pattern, and it stands on legs of stainless steel with a warm metallic finish. The tight upholstery keeps its line crisp, with no loose cushions to plump. Some assembly is required.

Place it in a dressing room or bedroom beside a mirror, in a living room opposite the sofa, or at a writing desk, with a small table close by for jewelry, a glass and the evening's tickets. This listing is for one armchair.
